An exact counting relationship with limits

Begin with the pair 1, 1. Each press applies the same rule: the first new number is twice the first old number plus the second; the second new number is the sum of the old pair.

The research connects this rule to particular tiling patterns through several mathematical steps. The ornament here is decorative. The counter shows the exact small calculation.

Apply the rule one step at a time. Watch the two numbers. Reset to begin again.

Words used here
transformation
A stated rule for changing one state, number pair or arrangement into another.
carrier
The particular thing being described by a model: for example, a set of numbers, a physical device or a system of relations. Shared mathematics does not make two carriers the same thing.
Read the fuller explanation

Start with the pair one, one. The declared action sends a pair to two times the first plus the second, and then the first plus the second. Each press applies the same integer matrix. Its counts grow while a precise relation remains available to inspect.

The source connects this two-state Fibonacci/Penrose action to a particular girih count construction through a quotient, normalization and lattice embedding. Those intermediate operations carry the evidence. Sharing a golden number would not supply them.

The rosette is decorative geometry, not a reconstruction of the historical artwork. The counter is the exact small calculation. Keeping ornament and result distinct allows both to be enjoyed on their own terms.

Girih inflation and the index-two scar

The two-state matrix [[2,1],[1,1]] is exact in the declared Fibonacci/Penrose count action. The published girih construction reaches a related iterate through additional operations. The displayed counts do not reconstruct a historical tiling or establish a physical carrier.
